title: Load Generation Past Saturation Without Offered-Load or SLA Limits
pattern: A load test drives requests as fast as possible without a target offered-load rate, an in-flight limit, or a latency SLA check, and reports the peak throughput reached.
why_bad: Beyond saturation, queues grow without bound and throughput numbers come with unusable tail latency (1M IOPS at 50 ms is worse than 990k IOPS within a 5 ms SLA). The headline number describes a state the system can never be operated in, and the run can exhaust client memory with unsent requests.
detection: A benchmark loop that submits async or fire-and-forget requests continuously without a rate limiter, without bounding outstanding requests, and without computing or checking a latency percentile against a threshold before reporting throughput.
counterexample: Stress tests whose stated goal is finding crash or overload-behavior thresholds, where throughput at the SLA is not being reported.
fix: Sweep offered load in steps with a rate limiter and bounded in-flight requests, and report the highest throughput at which the latency percentile still meets the SLA.
source: Richard L. Sites, *Understanding Software Dynamics* (2021), Ch. 11, p. 190; Brendan Gregg, *Systems Performance* (2013), Ch. 12, §12.3.7, p. 610.
